title: Throttle correlation datapull - model mix & region snapshot 2026-06-14
summary: Purpose: extract request- and scheduler-level telemetry to correlate throttle events with GPU saturation, model mix shifts, and regional failover during the June 12-13 capacity incident. This sheet captures the raw pulls, sampling heuristics, and initial anomalies for the postmortem. Goal is to produce a compact dataset for analysis and charts (per-region queue depth, throttle reason breakdown, model variant distribution) and to hand off to SRE and serving runtime for root-cause validation.
pull_objectives: Enumerate all throttle events and their immediate preceding queue depth and GPU util metrics
Attribute throttles to model family and serving tier (hosted/dedicated/private)
Measure region-level resource pressure and cross-region spillover counts
Capture scheduler preemptions, host reboots, and maintenance windows overlapping the incident
Provide time-aligned token/latency distributions for throttled vs non-throttled requests
queries:
-- Q1: request-level join of inference requests with throttle flags and token/latency metrics
SELECT r.request_id, r.request_ts, r.region, r.model_name, r.model_variant, r.customer_tier, r.seq_length_tokens, r.total_tokens, r.latency_p50_ms, r.latency_p95_ms, t.throttle_reason, t.throttle_ts, t.throttle_score, s.queue_depth_at_request, s.gpu_util_avg_60s, s.gpu_mem_used_mb, s.host_id, s.gpu_type
FROM telemetry.inference_requests r
LEFT JOIN telemetry.throttle_events t ON r.request_id = t.request_id
LEFT JOIN telemetry.scheduler_state s ON s.host_id = r.host_id AND ABS(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (r.request_ts - s.sample_ts))) < 30
WHERE r.request_ts BETWEEN '2026-06-11T00:00:00Z' AND '2026-06-15T00:00:00Z'
AND r.model_family IN ('redwood-xxl','open-llama-70b','mix-quant-13b')

-- Q2: per-host 1-minute rollups for utilization and active queues during window
SELECT sample_ts, host_id, region, gpu_type, active_pods, queued_requests, gpu_util_percent, io_wait_ms, preemptions_last_10m
FROM telemetry.host_minute_rollup
WHERE sample_ts BETWEEN '2026-06-11T00:00:00Z' AND '2026-06-15T00:00:00Z'
AND region IN ('us-west-2','eu-central-1','ap-southeast-1')

-- Q3: scheduler decision log around throttles to capture reason breakdown
SELECT decision_ts, decision_id, host_pool, model_family, requested_gpus, assigned_gpus, decision_outcome, outcome_reason, fallback_model_variant, queue_length_at_decision
FROM scheduler.decision_log
WHERE decision_ts BETWEEN '2026-06-12T08:00:00Z' AND '2026-06-13T20:00:00Z'
AND decision_outcome IN ('throttle','defer','assign_fallback')

-- Q4: cross-region reroute and spillover markers (when routing lifted to fallback region)
SELECT r.request_id, r.request_ts, r.origin_region, rr.reroute_ts, rr.target_region, rr.reason
FROM routing.reroute_events rr
JOIN telemetry.inference_requests r ON r.request_id = rr.request_id
WHERE rr.reroute_ts BETWEEN '2026-06-12T00:00:00Z' AND '2026-06-13T23:59:59Z'

-- Q5: recent capacity reservations/maintenance that overlapped incident
SELECT reservation_id, host_pool, region, reserved_gpus, start_ts, end_ts, owner, ticket_ref
FROM capacity.reservations
WHERE (start_ts <= '2026-06-13T23:59:59Z' AND end_ts >= '2026-06-11T00:00:00Z') OR ticket_ref IN ('OPS-891','MAINT-2026-06')
query_notes: Join heuristics: when matching request -> scheduler state, use a 30 second proximity to keep dataset compact (we sample nearest minute stamp)
Sampling: full pull for throttle_events, 1:20 sample for non-throttled requests to keep result size manageable; Q1 clause includes model_family filter to prioritize high-cost models
Fields 'throttle_score' are internal composite metrics (0-100) used by autoscaling policy; include for correlation analysis
Timezones: all timestamps normalized to UTC in the pulls
Retention: raw telemetry tables have TTL; ensure export to long-term bucket for postmortem artifacts
anomaly_findings: High concentration of 'capacity_overflow' throttles in us-west-2 between 09:00-11:00 UTC on 2026-06-12 with queue_depth spikes >120 requests
Model mix shift: sudden increase in redwood-xxl traffic (approx +42% relative to previous 24h) correlates with elevated throttle_score and fallback assignments
Two hosts (host-3a2, host-7f) showed repeated high GPU util (>95%) coincident with kernel OOMs in logs — investigate driver/kernel interaction
Multiple cross-region reroutes from eu-central-1 -> us-west-2 during incident peak, suggesting routing policy failed to respect regional capacity thresholds
A maintenance reservation (resv-449) overlapped the incident window in us-west-2 reducing spare capacity by 12 GPUs — not previously flagged as high risk
threshold_table: queue_depth:>100:expected high queue indicating saturation and likely throttles
gpu_util_avg_60s:>90%:sustained saturation window - investigate kernel/thermal/driver issues
throttle_score:>70:autoscaler likely to prefer fallback or throttle rather than wait
fallback_assignments:>5 per minute:unexpected fallback churn; may indicate mis-tuned routing policy
charts_suggested: Region timeline: stacked area chart of queued_requests vs assigned_requests per region (1-min resolution)
Per-model-family throttle rate heatmap (region x hour) to show where a single family caused pressure
Host-level scatter: gpu_util_avg_60s vs queue_depth_at_request colored by throttle_reason
Reroute flows: Sankey showing origin_region -> target_region counts during incident
Reservation overlap chart: reservations overlaid on regional free_gpu count
action_items: SRE: confirm whether host-3a2 and host-7f kernel OOMs map to specific driver versions; isolate and repro on staging by end of week (owner: Leo Zhang)
Serving runtime: add temporary stricter per-model ingress caps for redwood-xxl family in us-west-2 until autoscaler tuning is updated (owner: Rina Kaur)
Capacity planning: mark maintenance reservations that reduce spare capacity below 15% as 'high risk' and require approval from capacity leads (owner: Miguel Santos)
Routing: update reroute policy to respect 'soft-capacity' thresholds for target regions and add telemetry alert when reroutes exceed 50/min (owner: eng-routing)
Data: persist full throttle_event feed to long-term bucket for 90 days to enable future forensic queries (owner: infra-data)
Follow-up: schedule a 90-minute incident review session with product and platform next Tue to review user-facing impacts and COMMS
